hints.title: Timestamp Filtering
hints.text: Extract the hour component from order timestamps to isolate orders placed during the 18:00 window.

hints.title: Customer Aggregation
hints.text: Join customer profiles with the filtered orders and group by customer identifier and name.

hints.title: Total Spending Filter
hints.text: Apply a group filter clause to retain only customers whose aggregated golden hour spending reaches at least 100.

hints.title: Reference Implementation
hints.text:
```sql
SELECT 
    c.customer_id,
    c.name,
    SUM(o.amount) AS total_golden_spent
FROM Customers c
JOIN Orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
WHERE HOUR(o.order_timestamp) = 18
GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.name
HAVING SUM(o.amount) >= 100
ORDER BY c.customer_id ASC;
```

complexity.notes: Indexed date filtering followed by grouped aggregation.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Correlated scalar subqueries for each customer result in slow quadratic execution.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Grouping hash table bounded by distinct customer count.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Clean date extraction function and aggregate filtering via group filter clause.

    SUM(o.amount) AS total_golden_spent
FROM Customers c
JOIN Orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
WHERE HOUR(o.order_timestamp) = 18
GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.name
HAVING SUM(o.amount) >= 100
ORDER BY c.customer_id ASC;

SELECT 
    c.customer_id,
    c.name,
    SUM(o.amount) AS total_golden_spent
FROM Customers c
JOIN Orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
WHERE EXTRACT(HOUR FROM o.order_timestamp) = 18
GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.name
HAVING SUM(o.amount) >= 100
ORDER BY c.customer_id ASC;

import pandas as pd

def find_golden_hour_customers(customers: pd.DataFrame, orders: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    orders['order_timestamp'] = pd.to_datetime(orders['order_timestamp'])
    golden_orders = orders[orders['order_timestamp'].dt.hour == 18]
    grouped = golden_orders.groupby('customer_id')['amount'].sum().reset_index()
    qualified = grouped[grouped['amount'] >= 100]
    res = customers.merge(qualified, on='customer_id')
    res = res.rename(columns={'amount': 'total_golden_spent'})
    return res[['customer_id', 'name', 'total_golden_spent']].sort_values('customer_id')
